subject.title: Feature: durable natural-language rule learning + explicit multi-mention reply semantics

question: Should OpenClaw introduce a first-class durable conversational rule-governance layer and cross-channel explicit multi-bot mention semantics, or keep those as narrower memory-plugin/channel-plugin improvements?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses memory authority, storage, workspace file precedence, and channel delivery policy; code inspection shows current main has useful pieces but no settled product contract for the proposed layer.

options.title: Keep as design tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer-sponsored design that defines rule authority, storage, conflict precedence, and channel mention semantics before implementation.

options.title: Split into narrower work
options.body: Track Feishu self-mention loss and bot-to-bot delivery in focused channel issues/PRs, and open a separate memory-governance design issue only if maintainers want that product direction.

options.title: Route to plugin/API design
options.body: Require the durable rule-learning capability to prove it cannot be built through memory/plugin APIs before adding core rule-layer surface.

recommendation.title: Keep as design tracker
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer-sponsored design that defines rule authority, storage, conflict precedence, and channel mention semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest recent cross-surface contributor across memory docs, prompt/context, and Feishu runtime boundaries in the inspected history.
